resources.string:
This tab collects names worth checking by ear. They pile up while you listen, if “Collect names” is on (it is off by default). The “Names from a book” button (book icon next to the trash can) collects names from a book file (txt, fb2, fb2.zip, epub) right away, without reading it aloud.

Tap a word to add it to the stress dictionary: pick the stressed vowel and the list. An empty list “Names” is created for this, delete it if you do not need it. Or add the word to replacements, if the name should be spelled with «ё» instead of «е» («Курылев» becomes «Курылёв»). Swipe a word to hide it (in TalkBack, use the “Hide” action). It is no longer collected, and you can find it again with the “Hidden” checkbox, where a swipe or the “Unhide” action brings it back. The list keeps up to 2,000 entries, the oldest ones are dropped.

It collects capitalized words that are not at the start of a sentence and are not in the model dictionaries, the morphology table or your own lists: character names, surnames, place names. A name that is also an ordinary word (Паук “spider”, Верхушка “top”) is not collected. The model guesses the stress in an unfamiliar name and gets about one in three wrong, and how sure it is tells you nothing. That is why you have to check by ear.
No hidden words. A hidden word ends up here and is no longer collected during reading. To bring it back, swipe its row (in TalkBack, use the “Unhide” action).

Nothing here yet. Turn on “Collect names” at the top and listen to something for a while, the names will show up here. Tap a word to add it to a dictionary with the right stress, swipe it to hide it (in TalkBack, use the “Hide” action).
The word as it should be read: with «ё», with «+» before the stressed vowel
The words will disappear from this tab. Stress dictionaries, including the “Names” list, will not change.

The book file (txt, fb2, fb2.zip, epub) is scanned silently, and names are picked the same way as while reading aloud: capitalized words, not at the start of a sentence, with at least two vowels.

Words the model already knows are left out: those in its dictionaries and morphology table (Паук “spider”, Верхушка “top”, Москва “Moscow”), in your stress lists including the system one, and words you already hid here by swiping. The stress shown for each name is the model's guess, check it by ear.

New names are added to the list, not replacing it, up to 2,000 entries in total. Progress is shown in percent. You can stop at any time, and the names found so far are kept.
Add stress marks to a whole book

You do not need this to listen to books with RuVoice: stress is placed automatically while reading aloud, and a marked-up book may contain mistakes. This export is for other apps.

The book (txt, fb2, fb2.zip, epub) is processed the same way as text read aloud: your replacements, the text processing rules, stress dictionaries and choosing the stress by meaning. The result is saved as fb2 or txt. An fb2 keeps its formatting, footnotes and cover, while txt and epub become a plain fb2 split into paragraphs. Saved as txt, the book has only its text, one paragraph per line, without footnotes.

Words get stress marks, but the spelling stays as in the book. If a replacement changes how a word is spelled («нарошно», «ково-то», «н+аногу»), only the stress is taken from it. The only letters that change are «е» to «ё» where the model reads «ё», and «е» to «э» with “Hard «э» in loanwords” checked. Numbers, abbreviations and signs (№, %) are written out the way the model will say them, and acronyms in capitals only with “Spell out acronyms” checked. Words of one syllable get no mark. With “Stress only in homographs”, marks stay only where the stress depends on meaning: «за́мок» (castle) and «замо́к» (lock), «о́кна» and «окна́». The «ё» letters and written-out numbers stay everywhere.

A large book takes a long time. The screen stays on meanwhile, and you can stop at any time.
Loading stress models, this can take up to half a minute…
The selected book was lost while the file picker was opening. Please choose it again.

Rate and pitch multiply the values the reader app asks for. 1 means no change. Volume above 1 is louder than the model\'s own level, up to 3 times. Loud peaks are softened a little so the sound does not distort.
Speech rate and pitch from the Android settings. They apply to all apps and can only be changed on the system text-to-speech screen.

Lines of dialogue that start with a dash or a quotation mark can be read with a different voice, rate and pitch. Experimental: if the reader app sends text one sentence at a time, a line of dialogue longer than one sentence is recognized only where there is narration next to it («— сказал он», “he said”).

The voice “%1$s” comes from a different pack than the main voice, so dialogue is read with the main voice. Your choice is kept: once the main voice is from the same pack again, dialogue gets its own voice back.
This voice is linked to this profile, “%1$s”
This voice is linked to the profile “%1$s”
The voice “%1$s” is not on this phone, %2$s is used instead. Your choice is kept: reinstall its voice pack and the voice comes back.
Silence the engine adds to the audio. Zero means only the pause the model makes by itself.
The models take up memory while the engine is running. After this many minutes without requests they are unloaded, and the next request loads them again.
Disabled, the line was moved to the list “System: disabled”

A line of the built-in list “System” can be disabled by swiping it (in TalkBack, use the “Disable” action). It moves to the list “System: disabled” and stays disabled after app updates. Swiping it there (in TalkBack, the “Restore” action) brings it back.
Lines you disable in the system list will appear here. To bring a line back, swipe it (in TalkBack, use the “Restore” action).

Words where the engine puts the stress in the wrong place. Your entries win over the model\'s dictionary and its choice by context. If the stress depends on the neighboring words, add it on the Replacements tab as a phrase: «старый замок = старый з+амок» (“old castle”, read as за́мок, not замо́к, “lock”).

Replacements change the text before it is spoken. A key matches a whole word or phrase, ignoring case. Mark the stress with «+» before the vowel. In the edit window, the expandable “Stress” section shows the vowels of the word under the cursor, and tapping one inserts «+». An empty replacement or {skip} makes the engine skip the match.

«*» in the key matches any part of a word or a whole word: «прочита*», «*ходить», «нет * уже». The same «*» in the replacement puts back what it matched («программ* = прогр+амм*»). A replacement without «*» changes only the letters of the key: «туник* = тун+ик» reads «туника» as «тун+ика». If the same key appears twice, the last line wins. A comma in the key also matches when there is no space after it. «$» at the start of the key makes it case-sensitive («$Ворон» matches only the name Ворон, not the word ворон, “raven”). These rules are the same as in dictionaries for Demagog (a Russian program that reads text aloud), so such dictionaries can be imported as they are, from the “List actions” menu (⋮ next to the list name). A key starting with «~» is a regular expression (the dialog has a switch and help for it), and $1, $2 work in the replacement.

Markers (they also work right in the text being read):
{pause:300} is a pause in milliseconds. Between sentences it is silence, inside a sentence it works like a comma of that length and the intonation does not break.
*word* gives the word emphasis. Its strength is set in the More options menu (⋮) at the top right, under “Reading rules”.
{prosody:80:90} sets the rate to 80 percent and the pitch to 90 percent. It works from that point until {prosody} or the end of the paragraph. Example: «(шёпотом) = {prosody:80:90}» (“in a whisper”), everything after this note is read lower and slower. Pitch 0 gives a robot voice: «{prosody:100:0}».
List is on, used when reading
List is off, not used when reading
No slash or backslash, at most 60 characters
Delete the list “%1$s” (entries: %2$d)? This cannot be undone.
Regular expression rules skipped: %d, Demagog does not support them. Save them to a separate file?
Words where the engine puts the stress in the wrong place. To add a word, tap the “Add word” button (+) at the bottom.
Words and phrases to replace before speaking. To add one, tap the “Add replacement” button (+) at the bottom.
Put the cursor in a word to see its vowels, tap a vowel to insert «+»
Leave empty to skip this text when reading
Use $1, $2 for groups, write \\$ for a literal «$»
Replace the current settings, profiles, stress and replacement lists and the list on the Names tab with the contents of the file? You can undo this right after the import.

RuVoice is a speech synthesis engine. It does not read anything by itself, it gives a Russian voice to other apps. It reads only Russian text. English can be passed to another engine (More options menu (⋮) at the top right → “Reading English”), other languages it does not know.

First, whether you use a screen reader. A screen reader is an Android service for blind and visually impaired people (TalkBack, Jieshuo and others). It reads everything on the screen aloud and is controlled with gestures, and it is turned on in Android Settings → Accessibility. If you have never turned one on and use your phone the usual way, you do not have a screen reader.

Only listening to books, no screen reader

In your reader app (Moon+ Reader, ReadEra, Librera and others), choose the RuVoice TTS engine in the read aloud settings. If the reader app has no engine choice of its own and uses the system engine, make RuVoice the preferred engine (steps below). Then other apps that read aloud, a navigation app for example, will also speak with the RuVoice voice.

With a screen reader

The screen reader speaks with the system's preferred engine, so after the steps below the whole phone will speak with the RuVoice voice.

If your phone's interface is in Russian, make RuVoice the preferred engine. For the screen reader, there is a “Screen reading (TalkBack)” section in the More options menu (⋮) at the top right → “Reading rules”: special symbols read as words, no pauses and no silence before a phrase. Books are read as before.

If the interface is in another language, do not make RuVoice the preferred engine. The screen reader would read the whole interface with it, and RuVoice knows no other languages. Choose RuVoice only in your reader app. If the interface is in English and you still want RuVoice for the whole phone, turn on “Reading English”, then English text is read by another engine.

How to make RuVoice the preferred engine

1. Android Settings → System → Languages & input → Text-to-speech output (on Xiaomi: Additional settings → Languages & input, on some phones it is under Accessibility). The “Speech settings” button at the bottom takes you straight there.

2. Preferred engine → RuVoice TTS.

3. Android will warn that the engine “may be able to collect all the text that will be spoken, including personal data like passwords and credit card numbers”. This is the standard message for any third-party engine, the system shows it the same way for all of them. RuVoice has no internet permission and sends nothing anywhere: the model and speech synthesis run entirely on the phone.

Voice, pauses and dictionaries are set up here on the tabs, and the text processing rules are in the More options menu (⋮) at the top right → “Reading rules”. You can open this help again from the link at the top of the Voice tab and from the same menu.
How to enable the engine in Android
What to do when the problem is not in the engine but in the phone, the reader app or the system. More items will be added.
The start of a phrase is quiet and fades in, or sounds choppy

This comes from the phone\'s sound effects: Dolby Atmos, MiSound, the equalizer, “sound enhancement” and the like. Their volume leveling raises the volume gradually after silence, so the first word after a pause comes out quiet. Turn these effects off in the sound settings (button below), in the quick settings panel or in the headphone settings.\n\nThe “Silence before a phrase” switch also helps (on the RuVoice main screen, More options menu (⋮) at the top right → “Reading rules”). In the first fraction of a second after it starts, the Android audio player may swallow the beginning of the sound, and with silence in front, it is the silence that gets lost, not speech.
The sound stutters, the phone cannot keep up
On the Voice tab, set the sample rate to 24,000 Hz. Synthesis takes half the work, the player buffer is twice as long, and it sounds almost the same.
Reading stops and the system says RuVoice has stopped working

The button below copies a report: phone model, Android version, the latest crashes recorded by the system and a log of recent requests (with “Detailed log” on, it also contains the text being read). Send it to the author in the GitHub Discussions or the Telegram group, together with what was being read and with which settings.

The player gets audio only after a whole chunk of text is synthesized, so on a slow phone a long sentence can mean seconds of silence before the first word. The “Fast start in books and apps” rule in the “Miscellaneous” section helps (on the RuVoice main screen, More options menu (⋮) at the top right → “Reading rules”): the first chunk is cut to 100 characters and starts playing while the rest is being synthesized. If it is still slow, reduce “Maximum chunk length for books” in the same place.
Could not open the file for writing
Telegram group for announcements, questions and suggestions (in Russian):\nhttps://t.me/ruVoiceTTS
RuVoice is free, has no ads and will stay that way. If it has been useful to you and you want to say thanks, you can buy the author a coffee. This is optional and does not change anything in the app.
The latest version is always on the releases page, app stores may lag behind.

RuVoice TTS %1$s
Source code and new versions: https://github.com/kost-t-human/ruvoice-tts

Speech synthesis: Silero Models (github.com/snakers4/silero-models), model v5_5_ru, license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Non-commercial use only.

Stress: Silero Stress (github.com/snakers4/silero-stress), MIT license.

Morphological dictionary: AOT (github.com/sokirko74/morph_dict), LGPL license.

Speed change without pitch change: Sonic, Bill Cox, Apache-2.0.

A voice pack is a zip file with a Silero model and its voices (80 to 85 MB). Voices from a pack appear in the list on the Voice tab. Packs with other models (for example, cis_ru) have no question or exclamation intonation and no word emphasis.

Packs are in a separate release, “Паки голосов” (voice packs):
https://github.com/kost-t-human/ruvoice-tts/releases/tag/packs
No voices: this version of the app comes without a built-in model. Install the ruvoice-pack-ru.zip pack (the standard voices, about 85 MB) or any other pack.
The voices are being copied to the phone storage, this can take up to a minute. The window will close by itself.
Delete the pack “%1$s”? The model files will be erased. If one of its voices was selected, the default voice will be used instead.
What the engine does to the text before speaking it. A rule that is off leaves the text as it is. You can see the effect with “Analyze” on the Voice tab.
Maximum chunk length for the screen reader

A sentence longer than this is split at a comma or space and synthesized in parts. From 100 to 900 characters. Each part is synthesized as a whole, without stopping, so the screen reader has its own, smaller limit: a new screen reader phrase does not have to wait until a long part of the previous one is done.
TalkBack and other screen readers: Samsung, Huawei, Jieshuo, Dianming, anything that reads the phone screen aloud. These settings do not affect books and reader apps.

The first chunk of a screen reader phrase is at most 100 characters (cut at a comma), so the sound starts as soon as that chunk is synthesized, not the whole message. Otherwise a long chat message without periods, or with a link or emoji, means seconds of silence before it starts. Books have their own “Fast start in books and apps” rule in “Miscellaneous”.

Only for the screen reader: symbols such as arrows, the multiplication sign, @ and check marks are read by name, even if “Special symbols as words everywhere” in “Miscellaneous” is off. Books are not affected: there «* * *» and asterisk footnotes stay silent.

Only for the screen reader: an address starting with «https://» or «www.» is read as the word «ссылка» (link) and the site name («ссылка, youtube точка com»), instead of the whole address piece by piece. Works even if “Skip links” is on. Email addresses are read as before.
Lines starting with a dash in notifications and chats («— Привет») do not switch to the dialogue voice in the middle of a phrase.
The screen reader starts almost every phrase after a pause, so 300 ms of silence (the “Silence before a phrase” rule) would add a delay to every gesture.
Pauses after a sentence and after a paragraph (Pauses tab) are set to zero for the screen reader, so you can move through the screen faster. Pauses at commas and dashes stay.
Keep the model loaded while a screen reader is on

While TalkBack or another screen reader is turned on in the system, the model stays in memory, whatever the “Unload models when idle” setting (Pauses tab) says. Otherwise the first phrase after an idle period waits for the model to load. While the rule is active, the “Ready for the screen reader” notification stays up so the system does not close the engine, and the whole model is kept in RAM.
Remember screen reader phrases after restart

Short screen reader phrases («Кнопка» (button), «Назад» (back), app shortcut names) are saved as audio on the phone, up to 24 MB, and play right away even when the system has restarted the engine and the model is still loading. Turning this off deletes the saved audio.

While a screen reader is on, models are not unloaded, even if unloading is turned on above. The same setting is in the More options menu (⋮) at the top right, under “Reading rules”, “Screen reading (TalkBack)”.

Rate and pitch multiply TalkBack\'s own rate and pitch and are used instead of the Voice tab sliders. Volume multiplies the overall volume from the Voice tab. These sliders do not affect books. The resulting rate goes up to 6 times normal for the screen reader and 3 times for books.

The rules above apply only when a screen reader is speaking. It is recognized by the app that sent the text: TalkBack and other known screen readers, or any app with a speaking accessibility service turned on in the system. Below are the apps that have used the engine. When the switch is on, the app counts as a screen reader. If one was detected wrongly, flip its switch.
No app has used the engine yet. Turn on TalkBack, listen to a couple of phrases and open this screen again.
Not a screen reader, detected automatically (%s)
Not a screen reader, set manually (%s)

In all apps and in books. To have symbols named only for the screen reader, turn on “Special symbols as words” in the “Screen reading (TalkBack)” section above instead. Symbols the voice cannot pronounce by itself are read by name, as TalkBack does: the right arrow as «стрелка вправо», the multiplication sign as «знак умножения», @ as «собака», also triangles, the vertical ellipsis and check marks. In books «* * *» becomes «звёздочка звёздочка звёздочка». When off, such symbols are skipped, and a middle dot or an arrow between words gives a pause.

«Привет 😀» is read as «Привет, широко улыбается» (grinning face), «👍» as «большой палец вверх» (thumbs up), «🐱» as «морда кошки» (cat face). The names come from Unicode CLDR, as in Android. Skin tone is not read, and the same emoji repeated in a row is read once. Text emoticons too: «:)» and «спасибо))» as «улыбается» (smiling), «:D» as «смеётся» (laughing), «жаль((» as «грустит» (sad), «:blush:» as «краснеет» (blushing). When off, emoji are skipped and emoticons are read as punctuation.

A phrase made of one letter plus words like “deletion” or “capital”, which keyboards and screen readers send as you type or delete («Удаление заглавная Р», «р удалено»), is read with the letter name: «удаление, эр, заглавная», not a growled «ррр». For the screen reader this always works, this switch turns it on for books and other apps too. It applies only if the phrase has no other words. If “Single letter or symbol by name” is off, this does not happen anywhere.
Single letter or symbol by name

300 ms of silence before the first word, if more than 2.5 seconds have passed since the last sound. In the first fraction of a second after it starts, the Android audio player may swallow the beginning of the sound, and with silence in front, it is the silence that gets lost, not speech. Turn it off if the delay after a pause bothers you.

A request that is a single letter (in TalkBack: the letter under the cursor, typing echo, a key) is read as the letter name: «б» as «бэ», «ь» as «мягкий знак» (soft sign). A single symbol is read by name: «#» as «решётка». Letters that are words of their own inside text are not changed.
Fast start in books and apps

The first chunk of text is at most 100 characters (cut at a comma), the rest follow the length from the “Synthesis chunk length” section. Sound starts only after a whole chunk is synthesized, so on a slow phone a long sentence means seconds of silence before it starts. When off, the first chunk is like all the others. The screen reader has its own rule in “Screen reading (TalkBack)”.
Synthesize the next chunk in advance

The reader app queues the next chunk of text while the current one plays, but Android passes it to the engine only half a second before the sound ends. RuVoice sees such a chunk right away and synthesizes its beginning in advance, so the pause between chunks does not grow by the synthesis time. Works with reader apps that queue text in advance (AlReaderX and others), does not affect the screen reader.

Web addresses «https://…», «www.…» and «сайт.ru/…» are not read at all, including the path after the site name. When off, in books an address is read as the word «ссылка» (link) and the site name (the rule “Links in books as “link” and site name”), and if that rule is off too, piece by piece: «гитхаб точка ком слэш …».
Links in books as “link” and site name

For books and apps: an address is read as the word «ссылка» (link) and the site name without «www.» and the rest of the address («ссылка, youtube точка com»), instead of the whole address piece by piece. If “Skip links” is on, the address is skipped. Email addresses have their own rule. The screen reader has its own rule in “Screen reading (TalkBack)”.
Addresses like «mail@example.com» are not read at all. When off, they are read like «мейл собака ексампл точка ком».
The marker «(- Иллюстрация -)» that AlReaderX puts in place of a picture is not read. When off, you hear «Иллюстрация» (illustration).
Links and email piece by piece

When the address is read in full (the rule “Links in books as “link” and site name” and, for the screen reader, “Links as “link” and site name” are off), «ya.ru/page?id=42» is read as «йа точка ру слэш пейдж вопрос ай ди равно четыре два». When off, the address is read haphazardly and the digits in it are left as they are.

«21» is read as «двадцать один», «3,5» as «три целых пять десятых», «10 %» as «десять процентов», also the № and § signs. A basic rule: without it digits drop out of speech and the other number rules do nothing.

Russian numbers change form with grammatical case and gender. The form is chosen by the preposition or the neighboring word: «около 500 рублей» gives «пятисот», «1 книга» gives «одна», «2 книги» gives «две», «с 5 друзьями» gives «пятью». Gender and case of the neighboring word come from the morphology table: «1 ночь» gives «одна», «7 гномам» gives «семи», «последних 20 лет» gives «двадцати».
When a clue word is next to them, or when the numeral is written in capitals: «XX век» (century) is read as «двадцатый», also «глава IV» (chapter), «том II» (volume).
«Николай II» is read as «Николай второй», «Екатерина II» as «вторая».
«05.12.2020» is read as «пятого декабря две тысячи двадцатого года», «12.05» as «двенадцатое мая».
«20 июня» is read as «двадцатого июня», «к 1 сентября» as «к первому сентября».
«в 1917 году» is read as «в тысяча девятьсот семнадцатом», also «1941–1945 гг.», «в 90-х», «490 г. до н. э.».
«в 21:30» is read as «в двадцать один час тридцать минут». Only with a preposition or a word like «утра/вечера» (a.m./p.m.) nearby, so a Bible reference like «Иоанна 3:16» is left alone.

«+7 012 345-06-78» is read as «плюс семь, ноль двенадцать, триста сорок пять, ноль шесть, семьдесят восемь». In groups, keeping leading zeros. Covers numbers of Russia and neighboring countries, «8 (…)», numbers written without spaces and local ones like «123-45-67».

«Ваш код: 482913» (your code) is read as «четыре восемь два, девять один три». SMS codes, passwords, PIN and CVC are read digit by digit if the word «код», «пароль» or «PIN» is nearby. A card number «1234 5678 9012 3456» and «•• 1234» are read digit by digit, in groups.
км, кг, м², мин, ч, л and others: «около 3 км» is read as «около трёх километров», also «с 2 до 5 км».
«−5 °C» is read as «минус пять градусов цельсия», «°F» as «по фаренгейту».
«5 руб. 30 коп.» is read as «пять рублей тридцать копеек», also $, € and ₽.
«3/4» is read as «три четвёртых», «1/2» as «одна вторая», «25/3» as «двадцать пять дробь три».
Teaspoons and tablespoons in recipes: «2 ч. л.» is read as «две чайные ложки», «1 ст. л.» as «одна столовая ложка».
«2.10.3» is read as «два точка десять точка три». Two numbers with a dot («1.2») stay a decimal or a date.
«2 + 3 = 5» is read as «два плюс три равно пять», also the multiplication and division signs, «^» and a minus before «=».
«12 345 678» and «1 200 000» are read as one number, not as separate groups. When off, each group of digits is read separately.
Footnote marks like «[1]», «[12]» are removed from the text. When off, they are read as numbers.

«стр.» is read as «страница», «см. рис.» as «смотри рисунок», also «5 тыс. руб.», «г. Москва» as «город», «т. е.», «и т. д.». «гос. службы» becomes «государственной» when the gender and case of the next word are unambiguous.
Spelled letter by letter: «ФСБ» as «эф эс бэ», «МГУ» as «эм гэ у», «ЛКИ» as «эл ка и». When off, the model reads them its own way.
Spelled letter by letter: «USB» as «ю эс би», «FBI» as «эф би ай».

The letter is read by its name: «5800X» as «пять тысяч восемьсот экс», «5800X3D» as «… экс три ди», «GPT-4o» as «… четыре оу», «1080p» as «… пи». Cyrillic codes too: «Р-9» as «эр девять», «8К74» as «восемь ка семьдесят четыре».
Read the Russian way by transliteration: «iphone» as «айфон», «sherlock» as «шерлок». When off, words in Latin letters drop out of speech.
Latin letter in a Russian word
«прoблема» typed with a Latin «o» (a keyboard layout slip) is read as a normal Russian word.
English via another engine: books and apps
English words and phrases from reader apps and other apps are read by another speech engine installed on the phone, and their text is passed to it. Russian text stays with RuVoice.
English via another engine: screen reader
The same for TalkBack and other screen readers: menu items, buttons, messages in English. Turned on separately from books, you can turn on both.
Default: an offline voice, if the engine has one
Default. The engine has no offline voice for English, so the text may be sent over the internet. Download an English voice in the engine settings.
Choose an engine for English first.
The engine no longer has the selected voice (%1$s), so English is read with the default voice. Choose a voice here.
Asking the engine for its voices…
The engine “%1$s” has no English voices. You can download them in that engine\'s own settings.
Minimum words in a row in books
Minimum words in a row for the screen reader

Books and apps: how many English words in a row inside Russian text are needed before the other engine reads them. 1 means any English word. With 2, single words like «iPhone» stay with the Russian voice, with 3 also two-word names like «Microsoft Word». Text that is entirely in English always goes to the other engine. Abbreviations in capital letters («USB», «OK») and Roman numerals are read in Russian. From 1 to 10.
Screen reader: the same for TalkBack and other screen readers. Menu items and buttons are usually short, so the default is 1. From 1 to 10.
Wait for the English engine, ms

Screen reader: if the English engine has not answered within this time (including connecting to it), the phrase is read by the Russian voice so the screen reader is not left silent. After such a failure, English is read by the Russian voice right away for one minute, without waiting, and then goes to the English engine again. Lower is more responsive, but on a slow phone falls back to the Russian voice more often. Default is 2500 (2.5 seconds), from 500 to 10000. Books wait longer, they do not need this.

Adjustments for English on top of the overall rate and volume: the same rate sounds different in two engines. English volume is matched to the Russian voice automatically, the slider makes it louder or quieter on top of that.
There are no other speech engines on the phone. English is read by the Russian voice, as before.
Not chosen, English is read by the Russian voice. Choose an engine or turn the switch on again.
The selected engine is no longer on the phone, so English is read by the Russian voice. Another engine is not picked automatically, choose one here.

English phrases will be read by “%1$s”. RuVoice itself still works without the internet, but the text of these phrases is passed to that engine.

If it has no offline English voice downloaded, it may send the text over the internet. An offline voice can usually be downloaded in that engine's own settings.

Russian text stays on the phone and is read as before.
«со-» at the end of a line and «бака» at the start of the next are joined into «собака». Hyphenated words like «Санкт-Петербург» and «по-русски» are left alone.
A single line break before a lowercase letter (common in text from PDF files) is treated as a space, not as a new paragraph. When off, each line is a separate paragraph.
«!!!» becomes «!», «. . .» becomes «…», a hyphen with spaces around it becomes a dash. When off, «Всё. . . Дальше» is split into sentences at every dot.

, , and (also inside a sentence, without breaking it; pitch=\"robot\" gives a flat robot voice). When off, text with tags is read as it is.

In Russian the stress of a word can depend on its case. A word after a preposition, a number or an adjective that agrees with it gets the stress of its case: «вдоль стен+ы», «в ст+ены», «за сел+о», «две рук+и», «высокие ст+ены», «высокой стен+ы». «все» before a plural noun is read as «вс+е»: «вс+е окна». When off, the neural network decides.
Plural at the start of a sentence

Some words are spelled the same in the plural and in another form but stressed differently. At the start of a sentence they are read as plural: «Стр+елы летели» (the arrows flew), «Гл+аза блестели» (the eyes shone). Without a verb nearby the neural network would pick «стрел+ы» (of an arrow). The list has 31 words (глаза, руки, слова, губы, ноги, стены, стрелы, письма, реки…) that are read as plural in 98 percent of such cases in books. Does not apply if a negation or a singular adjective follows. When off, the neural network decides.

For words whose stress depends on meaning, the neural network picks the stress from context: «старый з+амок» (old castle), «дверной зам+ок» (door lock). When off, such a word is read like any other word.

A separate stress neural network places the stress in every word. When off, stress comes only from the built-in exceptions dictionary and your dictionaries, and the voice reads the other words its own way, usually worse.

Russian texts often print «е» instead of «ё». Words where «ё» is certain (ёжик, ещё, зелёный, from the eyo dictionary, 106 thousand word forms) get it before the neural network runs. Ambiguous ones (все/всё, небо/нёбо) are left to the model. When off, only the model puts in «ё».

In some borrowed words the consonant before «е» is pronounced hard, as if written «э»: тест is said «тэст». Such words (энергия, тест, компьютер, проект, a Wiktionary list based on the pronunciation dictionary, about a thousand words with their derivatives) get «э» after the stress is placed. When off, the model reads «е» soft.
Hyphen after a prefix read as a space

«Из-под», «по-другому», «во-первых» are sent to the model as «из под», «по другому»: the model stretches a hyphen into a pause, and with a space it sounds smoother. Only for the unstressed prefixes во-, по-, из-. «кто-то», «чёрно-белый» are left alone. When off, the hyphen stays, as in the text.
Period after a phrase without final punctuation

The model drags out the last vowel, and without punctuation at the end the stress moves onto it: «страдала» sounds like «страдалá». A chunk without a final mark (a single word, a menu item) is sent to the model with a period, without adding a pause. A word stressed on its last syllable is left alone. When off, the text goes as it is.
No period after a stressed final syllable

Before a period the model swallows the last vowel, so stress on the last syllable is heard on the one before it: «ухо востро» sounds like «вóстро», the same with «светло», «окно». When on, such a word at the end of a sentence is sent to the model without the period. The stress is heard better, but the voice drops less at the end of the phrase. When off, the text goes as it is.

«— Да.», «Вы?», «Кто?», «Всё.»: a word of 2 or 3 letters ending in its only vowel, when it is the only word in the sentence. The model says such a vowel in 160 ms, and when sped up you hear just «Д\'». The rule doubles the vowel (about 300 ms). When off, the text goes as it is.
Questions («Ты идёшь?», «Чай или кофе?») and exclamations are read with matching intonation. When off, everything is read as a statement.
A word in asterisks («Он *не* пришёл» in the text or in a replacement, <emphasis> in SSML) is stressed by the model with intonation. When off, the asterisks are just removed.
From 1 to 3: 1 is slightly stronger than the neighboring words, 3 is the strongest. Applies to all emphasized words.
«Эй, вы!», «Бам!» (up to two words ending in «!») are read with emphasis on the last word, otherwise the model says them short and flat. Strength is the same as for word emphasis above.
Emphasis in a question without a verb

«Вы барон Гордеев?», «Это правда?»: a yes/no question without a verb is read with emphasis on the last word. Otherwise the model raises the voice on the first word and drops it at the end, and the question sounds like a statement. A question with a verb («Ты придёшь завтра?») is left alone. Strength is the same as for word emphasis above.
The “After a comma” pause from the Pauses tab is also added after semicolons and colons.
Parentheses are read as commas: «дом (тот) стоит» is read as «дом, тот, стоит», with the “After a comma” pause. When off, parentheses just disappear and the words inside run into the phrase.

The model itself leaves some silence at the end and start of a sentence, and its length varies. With this rule the “After a sentence” pause (Pauses tab) is not added on top but is the minimum: the model\'s silence counts toward it, only the rest is added, and silence at the start of the next sentence is trimmed. Pauses come out more even. With a zero pause it changes nothing. Dialogue lines starting with a dash are not affected.

For tracking down problems. The log (it goes into the report from the “Copy report” button on the Troubleshooting screen) records the text of every request from the reader app (invisible characters and stress marks as codes) and what was sent to synthesis, with stress. “Analyze” shows which step placed the stress and the stress probabilities for each vowel. Screen reader phrases are not logged. When off, the log has only the time and duration of requests.

Synthesis runs only on the fast processor cores, the slow ones are not used. On phones with cores of different power, phrases are synthesized faster and use less battery this way: on a Redmi Note 13 5G, all 8 cores take twice as long per phrase as the four fast ones. When off, synthesis runs on all cores.

A profile remembers all settings: voice, rate, volume, pauses, rules, which dictionaries are on. Changes on the tabs and in “Reading rules” go to the selected profile. The dictionaries themselves are shared by all profiles. You can also switch profiles with the “RuVoice profile” tile in Quick Settings. A profile linked to a voice turns on by itself when that voice is chosen in the reader app or on the Voice tab. “Main” cannot be deleted.
